title: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials (Machine-to-Machine)
subtitle: A service authenticates as itself — no user, no browser, no front channel. Every hop here is server-to-server, so there is nothing to watch in a Network tab.

steps.label: Service needs an access token
steps.lede: A daemon, job, or backend service wants to call an API as itself. There is no human and no browser — this whole flow is a back channel.
steps.devtools: Nothing here is browser-visible, so DevTools does not apply. Observe the calls with a debugging proxy (mitmproxy / Charles / Fiddler / Burp) pointed at the service’s HTTPS traffic, with curl -v, or from the service’s own logs — never logging the secret or the full token.

steps.label: Request a token at /token
steps.lede: The client posts grant_type=client_credentials and authenticates itself — here with HTTP Basic (client_secret_basic). It asks for the scopes it needs.
steps.devtools: A server-to-server call — the engine flags it as back-channel. The Authorization: Basic header decodes to client_id:client_secret (svc-report-runner:cs_synthetic). Alternatives to Basic are private_key_jwt (a signed client_assertion) or an mTLS client certificate.

steps.label: Access token returned
steps.lede: The IdP authenticates the client, checks it is authorized for the requested scopes, and returns a bearer access token. Note there is no id_token and no refresh_token — there is no user.

jwt.title: Decoded access_token (this AS issues a JWT)
payload: Subject — the CLIENT itself; no human user
Audience — the resource server this token is for
Granted scope — may be narrower than requested

steps.devtools: Confirm the granted scope — it can be narrower than requested, and the client must check. Note sub == client_id: the workload is both caller and subject. Some ASes issue opaque access tokens instead, which carry no readable claims and are validated at the /introspect endpoint.

steps.label: Call the API with the token
steps.lede: The client calls the resource server, presenting the access token as a Bearer credential.
steps.devtools: Also back-channel. The API validates the token before returning data: signature via the IdP JWKS (or /introspect for opaque tokens), then iss, aud (itself), exp, and the required scope.

steps.label: Resource returned
steps.lede: The token checks out, so the API returns the data.
steps.devtools: On an expired token the API returns 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token". The client then refetches a token (previous step) and retries once.

steps.label: Cache the token until near expiry
steps.lede: The client caches the access token and reuses it across calls until it is close to expiring, rather than fetching a new one per request.
steps.devtools: There is no refresh token in this grant — when the access token expires the client simply repeats the /token request. Bad credentials return 401 invalid_client; an unauthorized scope returns 400 invalid_scope.
